steps.explanationAfterStep: An 8π electrocyclisation: eight electrons, a 4n system, so on heating the ends turn the same way (conrotatory). From the (E,Z,Z,E)-tetraene that puts the two methyl groups trans on the new σ bond: trans-7,8-dimethylcycloocta-1,3,5-triene. Huisgen saw it happen below room temperature (about −10 °C). The app does not check stereochemistry yet, so the drawings carry no wedges.

title: 8π Electrocyclisation of a tetraene
subtitle: A decatetraene closes conrotatory to a cyclooctatriene
references: Clayden, Greeves and Warren, Organic Chemistry, 2nd edition (Oxford University Press), chapter 35
Fleming, Pericyclic Reactions, 2nd edition (Oxford Chemistry Primers, Oxford University Press)
Huisgen, Dahmen and Huber, J. Am. Chem. Soc., 1967, 89, 7130

tetraene.caption: (2E,4Z,6Z,8E)-deca-2,4,6,8-tetraene, drawn curled so its ends meet
hintTiers: Eight π electrons in a chain of eight carbons. A σ bond forms between the two end carbons of the tetraene (the ones carrying the methyl groups): what happens to the four π bonds?
One new σ bond between the end carbons; the three π bonds left shift one place along each. Four arrows.

Arrow 1: from the first C=C π bond to a new bond between the two end carbons. Arrows 2–4: from each of the other three π bonds to the bond on its left (counting from the end used in arrow 1), so the new C=C bonds sit between carbons 2–3, 4–5 and 6–7.
tetraene.learnerPrompt: The two ends of the tetraene join to make an eight-membered ring. Draw the single step.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: That makes a six-membered ring and leaves a π bond outside it. In this first step all eight π electrons take part: the ring closes between the two carbons at the ends of the tetraene.
The methyl carbons have no π electrons and take no part. The ring closes between the two carbons carrying the methyl groups.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Right: the ends join. The carbon next to the new bond has lost its π bond, so each of the other three π bonds moves one place along in the same step. Three more arrows.

conditionsLabel: about −10 °C (the tetraene is made cold and closes as it warms)
mechanismSummary: Conjugated tetraenes close to cycloocta-1,3,5-trienes by an 8π electrocyclisation. With eight electrons (4n) the thermal reaction is conrotatory, so the (E,Z,Z,E)-dimethyltetraene gives the trans-dimethylcyclooctatriene. That triene does not stop there: at room temperature its own hexatriene unit closes in a 6π disrotatory electrocyclisation to cis-fused bicyclo[4.2.0]octa-2,4-diene (methyls still trans). The second closure is not drawn here: the app cannot yet offer a new bond that would make a four-membered ring in the same molecule. The same 8π-conrotatory, 6π-disrotatory pair runs in nature in the endiandric acid cascade. Rule of thumb, thermal: 4n electrons conrotatory, 4n + 2 disrotatory; under light both swap. The app does not check stereochemistry yet, so the drawings carry no wedges.
